title: Why was Salvador Brazil’s first capital?
hook: When the captaincies failed, Portugal needed a seat of government.
summary: Salvador was founded in 1549 by Tomé de Sousa as the seat of the colonial government, and it stayed the capital until 1763.

cardBlocks.text: At first, Portugal tried to colonize Brazil by splitting the coast into hereditary captaincies. The plan collapsed, and the Crown took the job on itself with a General Government. On 29 March 1549, the first governor-general, Tomé de Sousa, founded Salvador on a small peninsula between the Bay of All Saints and the Atlantic Ocean.

The city was meant to centralize Portuguese rule in the Americas and ease trade with Africa and the Far East. It grew fast, becoming Brazil’s main seaport and a major centre of the sugar industry and of the trade in enslaved people. It stayed the capital for more than two centuries, until 1763.
Salvador was founded in 1549 as the seat of colonial government and was Brazil’s capital until 1763.

deepDiveBlocks.text: Salvador’s centre was built to defend itself. The Upper Town, with defensive, administrative and residential roles, sits on top of an 85-metre escarpment.
His expedition had six ships and brought about a thousand people. Tomé de Sousa governed from 1549 to 1553.
From 1558, Salvador also had a slave market: Africans were brought there by force to work on the sugar plantations. In 1985, the Historic Centre of Salvador was added to UNESCO’s World Heritage List.
